L14@P0: Abstract: The periodic discrete Toda equation defined over finite fields has been studied. We
L15@P0: obtained the finite graph structures constructed by the network of states where edges denote
L16@P0: possible time evolutions. We simplify the graphs by introducing a equivalence class of cyclic
L17@P0: permutations to the initial values. We proved that the graphs are bi-directional and that they
L18@P0: are composed of several arrays of complete graphs connected at one of their vertices. The
L19@P0: condition for the graphs to be bi-directional is studied for general discrete equations.
L20@P0: MSC2010: 37K10, 37P05, 37P25, 37J35
L21@P0: Key Words: integrable system, discrete Toda lattice, finite graph, finite field
L22@P0: 1. Introduction
L23@P0: The Toda lattice has first been introduced as a mechanical model of the chain of particles with
L24@P0: nonlinear interaction force by springs [1]. Toda has discovered that the nonlinear system

L38@P1: discretization (fully-discretized version) of the Toda lattice has been obtained [3, 4]. Its generalization
L39@P1: and the proof of complete integrability has been done by Suris [5, 6]. We focus on the fully-discretized
L40@P1: Toda lattice equation in [4] in this article, and study the behavior of the solutions of the equation
L41@P1: over finite fields. Study of the integrable equations over finite fields is of importance for the following
L42@P1: reasons. First, as each variable is allowed to take only finite number of values, it is easy for us to
L43@P1: obtain the result numerically without errors. Second, the system over finite fields can be naturally
L44@P1: seen as an analogue of a cellular automaton. The cellular automaton is a discrete dynamical system
L45@P1: the cell of which takes only a finite number of states [7]. Studying the discrete systems over finite
L46@P1: fields can provide fundamental models in analyzing cellular automata and so-called ultra-discrete
L47@P1: systems. However, the time evolution of the system is not always well-defined over finite fields: we
L48@P1: observe that the evolution comes to a stop as division by 0 mod p or indeterminacies appear for
L49@P1: most of the initial conditions. To study the system over finite fields we have either to rewrite the
L50@P1: equations so that they do not have division terms, or to extend the domain of definition so that the
L51@P1: equation is well-defined. The latter approach of extending the domains is studied in connection with
L52@P1: the dynamics over the field of p-adic numbers in one-dimensional case. In particular, discrete versions
L53@P1: of the Painlev´e equations has been studied [8]. Na¨ıve application of this method to two-dimensional
L54@P1: lattices such as the discrete Toda equation, discrete KdV equation has a certain difficulty, because
L55@P1: they have infinitely many singular patterns. In this article we adopt the former approach and aim
L56@P1: to understand the structure of the solutions of two-dimensional lattice equations over finite fields. In
L57@P1: the following sections, we consider the time and space discrete Toda lattice equation over the finite
L58@P1: field Fp := {0, 1, 2, ··· ,p − 1}, where p ≥ 2 is a prime number. The discrete Toda equation over finite
L59@P1: fields has been investigated by one of the authors, and there the solutions for several symmetric initial
L60@P1: conditions have been obtained [9]. This article further generalizes his result and presents the graph
L61@P1: structures of the solutions for general initial conditions. The states of the discrete Toda equations are
L62@P1: connected by the time evolution, and the pairs of states (vertices) and the connections (edges) form
L63@P1: finite graph structures. One of our results is that this graph is always bi-directional, if we consider
L64@P1: the equivalence class of states in terms of cyclic permutations of the variables. The other result is
L65@P1: that this graph is composed of finite number of complete graphs (polygons with all the vertices) that
L66@P1: are connected by one of their edges. We have presented several orbits for small primes and small sizes
L67@P1: of the system, and have also given a conjecture on the connected components of the graph for N = 2.
L68@P1: In the last section, we study in a generalized settings, which include the discrete Toda equation, and
L69@P1: obtain a sufficient condition for the graphs to be bi-directional.
